label: A_descriptive_spatial_association
explanation: Cross-sectional spatial association between Chinese stock, service infrastructure, and stock change is fully measurable with available data.
requirement_for_stronger_causal_claim: none beyond clean measurement and spatial-error handling

label: B_temporally_ordered_association
explanation: Temporal ordering X(2023) -> M(2024) -> Y(2024-12 to 2025-06) is achievable because the panel has 2024-12 and 2025-06 points; requires M to be a true 2024 stock (A-class licensed-registry sources).
requirement_for_stronger_causal_claim: M measured as observable-by-2024 stock, not current snapshot; Y window strictly after M

label: C_mechanism_consistent_evidence
explanation: Mechanism (service infrastructure lowers settlement frictions) can be argued and probed with subcategory and dose-response patterns, but not proven.
requirement_for_stronger_causal_claim: subcategory heterogeneity tests; placebo services; pre-trend checks

label: D_causal_mediation
explanation: Formal mediation (X -> M -> Y) needs exogenous variation in M and strong no-unmeasured-confounding assumptions not currently met.
requirement_for_stronger_causal_claim: panel service data; quasi-experiment or IV for M; sensitivity analysis

label: E_causal_effect
explanation: A clean causal effect of service infrastructure on stock change is not identified with a single cross-section of M and observational stock.
requirement_for_stronger_causal_claim: exogenous service shock or policy change; DID or event study; IV

label: omitted_variable_bias
explanation: Unobserved local amenities/co-ethnic demand drive both service location and stock change.
requirement_for_stronger_causal_claim: richer controls; municipal fixed effects in panel; IV

label: reverse_causality
explanation: Prior Chinese stock attracts services (X -> M) while services attract stock (M -> Y); single cross-section cannot separate directions.
requirement_for_stronger_causal_claim: strict temporal lags; lagged-M design; panel with leads/lags

label: anticipatory_service_location
explanation: Services may locate in anticipation of expected future Chinese growth, biasing M-Y association upward.
requirement_for_stronger_causal_claim: pre-trend tests; control for expected growth; event-study leads

label: common_trend_shared_shock
explanation: Region-wide trends (post-COVID rebound, visa-policy shifts) move services and stock together.
requirement_for_stronger_causal_claim: time/prefecture fixed effects; DID with comparison group

label: spatial_selection_bias
explanation: Self-selection of migrants into already-serviced municipalities confounds M-Y.
requirement_for_stronger_causal_claim: selection controls; IV; matching on baseline characteristics

label: timing_ambiguity_in_service_data
explanation: C_current_only sources lack reliable 2024 timestamps, so service existence by 2024 is uncertain; A-class registry dates mitigate this.
requirement_for_stronger_causal_claim: restrict M to A_2024_stock dated sources; verify license/designation dates

label: modifiable_areal_unit_problem
explanation: Municipality-level aggregation can change associations versus finer units (cho-chome).
requirement_for_stronger_causal_claim: robustness at alternative spatial units; sensitivity to boundaries

label: municipality_level_aggregation_bias
explanation: Within-municipality heterogeneity (ward vs suburb) is averaged away, attenuating mechanism signals.

label: registered_vs_actual_residence
explanation: ISA/MOJ registered address may differ from actual residence; affects both X and Y consistently.
requirement_for_stronger_causal_claim: acknowledge measurement scope; cross-check with Census where possible

label: zero_base_small_count_instability
explanation: 6 zero-base municipalities make percent change undefined and inflate log1p sensitivity.
requirement_for_stronger_causal_claim: retain zero_base flag; log1p with robustness; report absolute change
